notes.text: The Archive Inbox has a search box: find an archived ticket by number, Jira key, sender, subject or company.
Every piece of feedback you send now opens a ticket on the board for the support team, so it gets tracked and worked like any other ticket.
Admins can reassign a ticket to any support agent from "Who should take this" inside the ticket, not just to the people it suggests.

A frozen SLA now really stops: when the freeze is lifted, the timer picks up exactly where it was instead of coming back overdue. The same fix applies to snoozes, Waiting on Contact, Jira links and Velma bugs.
Every ticket that was frozen, or came out of a freeze, gets a fresh SLA. Tickets still frozen stay frozen and get their full time when released.
Every card now has a Spam button that sends the ticket straight to the Spam Inbox, along with other mail from the same sender. Restore it from the Spam Inbox if it was a mistake.
Tickets archived without being resolved no longer count in the KPIs. Tickets archived after being resolved still count as resolved work.
KPIs now update on time at 00:00, 09:00, 12:00 and 16:00 Tunisia time, and the page picks up each update even if your PC was asleep.
Admins have a Day report on the KPI page: every ticket resolved on a chosen day, by agent, with SLA met or missed.
When a ticket is reassigned to someone else, its SLA starts over, so the new owner gets the full time to answer. The badge says "since reassigned" when that is why the clock restarted.

Projects can now run on your own PC: once the runner is set up there, pressing Run hands the job straight to your Claude, with no tab to open and nothing to paste. While a run waits, the card tells you who is picking it up.
The My resolved count now matches the Resolved figure in your KPIs exactly, and updates at the same times. CS agents get it too, and admins get a Resolved chip for the whole team.
Patch notes now show up on the live board too, not just the test one.
Patch notes! Every board update now shows up here in the Feedback bubble, so you always know what changed.
A manual ticket created by an admin who is also a CS agent now gets them as its CS owner instead of Unassigned.
The board recognises your CS code wherever it appears on your account, not just in the first field it checks.
CS owner changes are sturdier: only agents on the CS roster can be picked, "No CS" sticks when chosen on purpose, and changing the CS owner no longer undoes a newer Support reassignment.
Select a whole column in one click: tick the box next to a column's count to select every ticket showing in it, then use the selection bar to act on all of them. Tick it again to unselect.
Tidier Feedback bubble header: the admin delivery Test button is gone.
New SLA baseline. The board clock now follows the server's time zone, and admins can put a ticket's SLA on hold.
Links in ticket notes are clickable and easy to copy, and notes can be edited after posting.
KPIs refresh four times a day: 00:00, 09:00, 12:00 and 16:00. Open SLA clocks reset to the baseline on their own.
Snoozed tickets now pause their SLA. Support agents can keep up to 5 tickets snoozed at once.
Reset the SLA on two tickets that were being timed wrongly.
Corrected an agent's resolved count in the KPIs, and the board no longer guesses a ticket's CS owner.
Admins can set who is on the CS and Support teams. The board asks before reopening a resolved ticket.
Resolved tickets no longer reopen on their own from stale data, and KPIs stay in sync in real time.
SLA history rebuilt back to launch day, so every KPI lines up.
Velma bugs are also looked up in a second sheet, and one agent's SLA met % was corrected.
Admins can change a ticket's CS owner straight from its card.
Welcome Terry Nyborg (TNY) and Levan Giunashvili (LGI) to the CS team!
The SLA pauses on weekends, outside working hours and during agent leave, on every screen.
The Velma sheet can be read without a Google sign-in.
Google sign-in for the Velma sheet is back as an option, and there is a public Privacy page.
Shift history survives updates, and an unknown SLA is no longer counted as met.
New My resolved view. Projects run through Claude with no API key, and emails are no longer copied to your clipboard by themselves.
Snoozed tickets no longer wake up straight away, and there are more snooze options. Everyone can edit manual tickets, and the CS owner can be picked on create.
Agents no longer need to sign in to Google to use Velma.
Admins can upload a service account key, so the Velma sheet loads without anyone signing in.
Behind-the-scenes tooling for the anti-churn service.
A fresh new look: violet-black chrome, stage colours and calmer cards. Garbled characters are fixed too.
The SLA resumes when a linked bug is marked DONE, and untagged tickets are shared out by priority.
Filter dropdown arrows no longer repeat across the control on hover.
Mark a teammate as off with a return date, and no tickets are assigned to them until they are back.
The Resolved KPI card counts only the selected date range, not all time.
Admins see every ticket since the board went live, with a new Since launch KPI range.
Google sign-in can be switched on from the board and opens in a new tab.
Link a ticket to a Velma bug. Tickets waiting on the contact get their SLA reset, and a ticket goes to the agent named in the email.
The SLA pauses while a ticket is in Jira and resets only on client replies. Closed tickets reopen when the client writes back, ticket numbers are never duplicated, and the board is easier to read.
The SLA freezes on Waiting on Contact, Support is alerted when CS sends a ticket back, and new tickets are shared across the team.
